review.scope: @UnstableApi is the Common [UnstableApi] attribute (source-only, as the Java SOURCE-retention annotation). The Java overrides that narrow the DefaultByteBufHolder return types are C# 9 covariant overrides ("an overriding method can declare a more derived return type", Microsoft Learn, Covariance and Contravariance in Generics). @UnstableApi is the Common [UnstableApi] attribute (source-only, as the Java SOURCE-retention annotation). CharSequence is ICharSequence, the CharSequence port of Common (AsciiString.Of(ICharSequence), codec-base Headers); a java.lang.String argument or result is passed as its ICharSequence wrapper StringCharSequence, whose equality and hash follow String (ordinal content, only against StringCharSequence). List<CharSequence> is IList<ICharSequence>; Collections.emptyList() is ReadOnlyCollection<T>.Empty and Collections.unmodifiableList(list) a ReadOnlyCollection<T> view. java.util.List equals/hashCode/toString (element-wise equality, 31*h + e.hashCode() from 1, "[a, b]") go through SmtpUtils.ListEquals/ListHashCode/ListToString because ReadOnlyCollection<T> keeps the Object members. CharSequence... is params ICharSequence[]; the package-private constructor taking a List is internal; checkNotNull throws ArgumentNullException.

Interface with the I prefix. @UnstableApi is the Common [UnstableApi] attribute (source-only, as the Java SOURCE-retention annotation). The Java re-declarations that only narrow a return type are inherited unchanged from the base interface, the Transport/Common rule "C# 9 covariant returns cover class overrides only" (docs/transport-porting.md); the implementing classes keep the narrowed return types. The interface field EMPTY_LAST_CONTENT is a static readonly interface field and its anonymous class the private nested class EmptyLastSmtpContent (C# interfaces may declare static fields and nested types); content() and refCnt() are the Content and RefCnt properties of the Buffer port, and the IByteBufHolder/IReferenceCounted members with wider return types are explicit implementations.

@UnstableApi is the Common [UnstableApi] attribute (source-only, as the Java SOURCE-retention annotation). CharSequence is ICharSequence, the CharSequence port of Common (AsciiString.Of(ICharSequence), codec-base Headers); a java.lang.String argument or result is passed as its ICharSequence wrapper StringCharSequence, whose equality and hash follow String (ordinal content, only against StringCharSequence). HashMap<String, SmtpCommand> is Dictionary<string, SmtpCommand> read with GetValueOrDefault; the static initializer is the static constructor. The package-private encode and isContentExpected are internal; name() stays a method; hashCode()/equals/toString are the BCL members, with the case-insensitive AsciiString hash and ContentEqualsIgnoreCase of Common.

The Java re-declarations that only narrow a return type are inherited unchanged from the base interface, the Transport/Common rule "C# 9 covariant returns cover class overrides only" (docs/transport-porting.md); the implementing classes keep the narrowed return types. The body is empty because every Java member is such a narrowing.

Interface with the I prefix; command()/parameters() stay methods. @UnstableApi is the Common [UnstableApi] attribute (source-only, as the Java SOURCE-retention annotation). List<CharSequence> is IList<ICharSequence>.

@UnstableApi is the Common [UnstableApi] attribute (source-only, as the Java SOURCE-retention annotation). Class<?> is Type, List<Object> out is IList<object> @out and IllegalStateException is InvalidOperationException (docs/codec-base-porting.md). IList<ICharSequence> is always indexable, so the RandomAccess marker test (no CLR counterpart) keeps only the indexed branch of writeParameters; the iterator branch for sequential lists has no input. ByteBufUtil.writeAscii(ByteBuf, CharSequence) has only the ReadOnlySpan<char> and AsciiString overloads in the Buffer port, so parameters are written from their ToString() text (same ASCII bytes). LeakPresenceDetector.staticInitializer, Unpooled.unreleasableBuffer/directBuffer and asReadOnly are the Common/Buffer ports.

@UnstableApi is the Common [UnstableApi] attribute (source-only, as the Java SOURCE-retention annotation). The final utility class with a private constructor is a static class. CharSequence is ICharSequence, the CharSequence port of Common (AsciiString.Of(ICharSequence), codec-base Headers); a java.lang.String argument or result is passed as its ICharSequence wrapper StringCharSequence, whose equality and hash follow String (ordinal content, only against StringCharSequence). The String results of the "FROM:<"/"TO:<" concatenations and help(String cmd) are StringCharSequence values; the conditional between a StringCharSequence and the AsciiString FROM_NULL_SENDER is typed ICharSequence explicitly; Collections.addAll is List<T>.AddRange and the local params is @params (C# keyword).

Interface with the I prefix; code()/details() stay methods. @UnstableApi is the Common [UnstableApi] attribute (source-only, as the Java SOURCE-retention annotation). List<CharSequence> is IList<ICharSequence>.

@UnstableApi is the Common [UnstableApi] attribute (source-only, as the Java SOURCE-retention annotation). decode(ctx, buffer) overrides the codec-base LineBasedFrameDecoder.Decode (protected internal there, protected from this assembly) with the covariant return type ISmtpResponse. CharsetUtil.US_ASCII is Encoding.ASCII and the String detail is a StringCharSequence; emptyList()/singletonList(x) are read-only collections. readByte() returns the unsigned System.Byte: the separator is compared only with ' ' and '-', so the branch is the same, but parseNumber keeps Java's (char) b, which sign-extends a byte to \uFF80..\uFFFF (JLS 5.1.4), through an sbyte reinterpretation, and Character.digit(ch, 10) is CharUnicodeInfo.GetDecimalDigitValue (decimal digits only, -1 otherwise). Numbers in messages use the invariant culture.

The package-private final utility class is an internal static class. CharSequence is ICharSequence, the CharSequence port of Common (AsciiString.Of(ICharSequence), codec-base Headers); a java.lang.String argument or result is passed as its ICharSequence wrapper StringCharSequence, whose equality and hash follow String (ordinal content, only against StringCharSequence). Collections.emptyList() is ReadOnlyCollection<T>.Empty and unmodifiableList(Arrays.asList(array)) is Array.AsReadOnly(array), a read-only view as in Java. The java.lang.String branch of validateSMTPParameter is the StringCharSequence branch (IndexOf); IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException. The internal ListEquals/ListHashCode/ListToString helpers carry the java.util.List contract used by DefaultSmtpRequest/DefaultSmtpResponse (Java SE List and AbstractCollection documentation, cited in the CLR comment).
